You know, deep down, that nicotine did nothing to enhance those moments. They were great because of the company or drinks or endorphin rush or whatever. Your nicotine addiction is warping your memories to get you hooked up again. 
But even if nicotine did enhance those moments, are they worth being trapped as a smoker just to enjoy them a little bit more? Are they so unpleasant as a non smoker to justify being addicted and throwing out all the progress you made to quit?

If you are planning on tapering off nicotine or cutting it cold turkey then yes. If you plan on consuming nicotine through vaping I think you are in real danger of smoking cigs again. But that’s just me. If it gives you confidence that it is working, keep at it.

Nice script. Some things were out of character for the boys though, but that shouldn’t get in the way of a good story. I think the ending is a bit overlong. Good work

Don't get me wrong, I think it's brilliant. The dialogues were great. Vert believable (except the Ginvid part, I'm pretty sure ship names weren't a thing in 1974). The other thing that kinda grated me was you giving the idea for a Syd tribute at the end of the funeral march to Roger. I think you were trying to paint him as the ideas man, and it works. But it is documented (on Mark Blake's book) that Rick came up with it unprompted.
The second nitpick that i have is that Roger and David knew each other from Cambridge and shared the same social group as Syd and Storm, so the first scene where they are musing about David could be changed into Roger defending or advertising David to the other 2.
Third and final nitpick. On a recent interview, David said that he regrets never actually telling Roger he was a good writer. They were quintessentially english in that they downplayed each others abilities. The most effusive Roger would get would be uttering "Well, I think we can get away with that" after a soul wrenching solo by David, for example (again, per Mark Blake's book). So the scenes where David consoles Roger.... It's just not them. 

And that's all i'll say or i'll be pushing my own vision on you. Keep at it, I loved reading it and hope to see the revised versions soon!
